title: Recursive Enhancement of Autonomous Agents Through Self- and Cross-Process Loop
content: Autonomous robots require learning, thinking, environmental interaction, and evaluation processes that continually build upon accumulated experience to develop their capabilities. However, existing approaches often rely on predefined process interactions and provide limited mechanisms for enabling individual processes to promote themselves or other processes through additional activities. This paper proposes Recursive Process Enhancement (RPE), a general framework that enables autonomous processes to periodically reuse their outcomes through self-loops and independently promote other processes through cross-process loops. RPE further introduces activity-driven loop amplification, in which valuable experiences or unresolved problems trigger additional thinking, learning, interaction, or evaluation activities without necessarily modifying the underlying algorithms. As a concrete realization, a thinking process generates positive, negative, and boundary counterfactual training materials from scarce high-value experiences. These materials are verified and incorporated into subsequent learning, while learning outcomes can guide further thinking and enhancement. Results from simulated autonomous-robot safety decisions over 12 random seeds show that RPE improves transfer Macro-F1 from 0.208 to 0.399 with one high-value experience and from 0.224 to 0.369 with two experiences, compared with continual experience replay.
